correctness.rationale: For any finite frame U containing 1, the exponential reindexing V_n=U^{b^n} is a valid finite-dimensional filtration because b^n+b^m<=b^{n+m}. Infinite dimensionality makes every adjacent power strict, yielding entropy at least log b. For k[x] the quotient dimensions are exactly (b-1)b^{n-1}, so entropy is log b while GK dimension is 1. The one-sided comparison and linear-control repair follow from U^n subset V_{sn}, the reverse linear inclusion, and subadditivity of log dim U^n.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2024 entropy paper already establishes filtration dependence and linear reindexing effects; those are explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. Targeted searches found no prior exponential-reindexing correction to arXiv:2609.18144v1, no matching k[x] counterexample to its arbitrary-filtration growth claims, and no identical one-sided/linear-control repair package.

value.rationale: The result corrects several central arbitrary-filtration implications in a new rings-and-algebras preprint, replaces an isolated contradiction by a universal acceleration mechanism, and identifies a concise quantitative hypothesis under which the intended growth conclusions are restored.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
